newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.7 pct to new 2-mth high.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.7 pct to new 2-mth high.

text.p: Istanbul shares gained an average 1.7 percent in hectic activity on Tuesday as a medium-term uptrend continued with the market testing new resistance at the index's 72,000 level, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 1,204.48 points, or 1.7 percent, higher at 72,051.24, a new two-month high after Tuesday. The previous highest close was 72,758.08 on July 11.
It had leapt 2.4 percent on Tuesday, after Monday's minor correction that followed last week's 7.3 percent surge.
"There was some selling today, but the market still looked good with the help of selective activity. It may try 73,000 levels tomorrow," said Huseyin Istanbullu from Meksa securities.
Brokers said activity again focused on shares of largely state owned firms which strongly move the market index with their large market capitalisations.
Trade volume leapt to 13.6 trillion lira from Tuesday's 12.4 trillion.
Brokers said selling triggered as the index neared the 72,000 barrier in the morning was followed by reaction buys, causing turnover to increase.
A medium-term uptrend was said to have started last week amid cash influx and market optimism.

The 85-share industrial index .ISEI leapt 1.79 percent to 79,148.38 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF firmed 1.46 percent to 63,605.52. Of the 225 issues traded, 96 rose, 70 fell and 59 finished steady.

Leading actives were utility Aktas Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 54,000 and largely state-owned firms -- petroleum refiner Tupras, steady at 15,750 lira, flat steel giant Eregli, up 300 lira at 10,500 and Turkish Airlines, steady at 30,500 lira.
